checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: fix the single generic 400 fix returned by every editor action, which answered 'no scene library is configured' with 'send a valid editor action with finite transform values'

impact_assessment.why: AI-driven game creation is a stated goal, and the HTTP API is how an agent drives the editor; unrelated advice stalls the loop.
impact_assessment.benefits: Each editor failure names the flag or action ordering that resolves it, and the advice is machine-actionable.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: fix strings change for 400 responses; dependency: none; concurrency: outer toolkit still edited; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Map each known failure family in _action_fix, verify derived flag names against --help, and assert the advice is sufficient by performing the recovery in a test.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Fixed and verified - _action_fix maps library, play-mode, prefab-mode, selection, batch and unknown-action causes; flag names checked against --help; save_scene with --scene-dir writes ai-built.kscene and load_scene reopens it; 1024 tests pass; 6/6 gates pass

[3/3] Probes that found no defect: /api/scene does reflect editor mutations (6 to 7 nodes with the new one present), so it is a live view rather than a stale snapshot; probe failures for materials and scene-doc were wrong expectations (no --material-dir, stale node id); checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-action-fix-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: close the single point-light limit (ADR-208 F5) by storing Scene.point_lights with a compatibility point_light property, a looped shader capped at MAX_POINT_LIGHTS=8, and list fields in snapshot, web scene, editor and schema

impact_assessment.why: Engine parity is now an explicit project goal; measured, a second lamp silently overwrote the first so two-light scenes were impossible.
impact_assessment.benefits: Levels can be lit with up to eight local lights and the editor can author them, while every existing single-light caller keeps working.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Scene field changes but point_light stays as a property; dependency: none new; concurrency: none; state: snapshot gains point_lights and still reads the legacy field.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Preserve the shader's attenuation and sRGB math exactly, prove single-light output byte-identical via the canonical hash and 4899B PNG, and pin two-light behaviour with a failing-first test.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Fixed and verified - Scene.point_lights with a point_light compatibility property; shader loops over 8 array uniforms; renderer, snapshot, web scene, editor set_scene and schema all carry the list; single-light output byte-identical (hash 772cac52..., PNG 4899B); 1035 tests pass

[3/3] Two-light proof: red-only luma 9.74, blue-only 9.69, both 11.24 with distinct hashes, centre pixel carries red and blue channels; 12 lights render without error; capping upload at one light makes the two-light test fail, so the guard is real; found and fixed a regression during the work where the legacy point_light branch was overwritten by the stale list; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-multilight-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add placed sprite nodes (ADR-208 F10) - a Sprite value type on Node, drawn through the existing billboard pass without requiring particles, with a per-instance tint so colour is not shared

impact_assessment.why: Sprites existed only for particles, so a glow or billboard sign had to be faked with a mesh; engine parity is an explicit goal.
impact_assessment.benefits: Scene content can be a camera-facing quad that follows the node transform, and the editor/snapshot can carry it.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Node gains a field and the sprite instance buffer widens; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: snapshot gains a sprite entry.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep particle rows at tint (1,1,1) so existing output is unchanged, verify the canonical hash and 4899B PNG, and pin render behaviour with failing-first tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented - Sprite(size,color,alpha) validated and set on Node; _draw_sprites walks the scene and no longer needs particles; instance buffer 5 to 8 floats with a_tint; snapshot writes and reads sprite; canonical hash unchanged and reference PNG still 4899B; 1051 tests pass

[3/3] Verified by rendering - one red sprite lights the centre pixel red while the empty scene lights none; red vs green differ so tint is per instance; alpha 0 and hidden draw nothing; size scales coverage 4 to 468 lit pixels from 0.2 to 3.0; node transform moves the sprite (centroid x 31.5 to 35.6); three render tests fail when the scene loop is removed; noted prefab and web set_node support as follow-ups; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-sprite-nodes-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: close the three paths that silently dropped Node.sprite - the web editor node document and set_node, the prefab document and instantiate, and the editor undo snapshot - by giving Sprite one shared to_dict/from_dict

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed an AI working over the web API could not create a sprite at all, and a prefab instance lost one on placement; AI-driven authoring is a stated goal.
impact_assessment.benefits: A sprite created over HTTP persists through undo, prefab capture, JSON round trip, instantiation and reload.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: set_node gains a field and the editor document gains a key; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: prefab and undo documents gain sprite.
impact_assessment.mitigation: One serialisation on the type, validation through the existing helpers, and failing-first tests for each of the four paths.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented - Sprite.to_dict/from_dict on the type; editor node document and undo snapshot carry sprite; set_node accepts a partial mapping or null with validation; prefab document, from_dict and instance clone carry it, and the override baseline records it; 1071 tests pass; canonical hash unchanged and PNG 4899B

[3/3] Verified - reach probe now reports 0 gaps across editor document, set_node, prefab document, instance clone and snapshot; partial set_node keeps size while changing alpha; null clears; undo drops the added sprite; four reach tests fail when the document and instance fields are reverted; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-sprite-reach-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: make the features added this session discoverable - --describe advertised neither point_lights nor sprite_nodes, the editor schema omitted sprite on node, SCENE_SCHEMA omitted it, and the scene export did not emit it

impact_assessment.why: A capability an AI cannot find in the discovery payload is absent for authoring; discovery is the first pillar of the project goal.
impact_assessment.benefits: An agent reading --describe or the schema finds both features and their field names without reading source.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: capability keys and schema field lists grow; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: scene export gains a key.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Take the light cap from MAX_POINT_LIGHTS rather than restating it, and assert the export actually emits the sprite the schema promises.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Fixed - describe_game reports sprite_nodes and point_lights (value from MAX_POINT_LIGHTS); EDITOR_SCHEMA and SCENE_SCHEMA list sprite on node; set_node allows it; web/scene.py now emits sprite so the declaration is true; 1075 tests pass; canonical hash unchanged and PNG 4899B

[3/3] Verified - a probe of --describe now lists point_lights and sprite_nodes; schema carries sprite in editor node, set_node and scene export; the scene export test proves the promised field is emitted; two discovery tests fail when the advertisement is removed; a systematic node-field coverage probe across snapshot, prefab and editor shows only parent/prefab_base/scene_group differences, all intentional; frame tracking and occlusion resolution probed and sound; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-discovery-v1' completed successfully.
